Backend.description: The backend that makes the network real. Only the Kernel backend exists in release 0.1.

oneOf.description: The backend is chosen by the tool: the Kernel backend in release 0.1.
Network namespaces, virtual Ethernet pairs and `netem`.

link.description: The values of every link, unless `links` has its own.

links.description: The values of each link in turn (one fewer than nodes), instead of `link`.

nodes.description: The nodes from one end to the other: at least two. The first link's forward direction is from the first node.

Chain.description: A line of nodes: the two ends are hosts, the nodes between them are routers, each pair is joined by a link.

both.description: A change of the impairments in both directions.

forward.description: A change of the impairments from the first node to the second.

reverse.description: A change of the impairments from the second node to the first.

Change.description: What `set` changes, for each direction. `both` changes the two directions.

env.description: Environment variables besides `NETSCENARIO_*`. Values may use `{node.addr}`.

kind.description: `command`: a program of your own in a node.

on-exit.description:
`continue` (default): the run goes on when the program ends by itself with an error. `fail`: the run is stopped
with an error.

ready.description: How the run learns that the program can be used.

run.description:
The program and its arguments, without a shell. `{node.addr}` is replaced by the address of a node;
a brace that is meant as a brace is written twice.

file.description:
The file of samples, one number per line (or several, separated by spaces or commas), a path relative to the
directory of the scenario file. Lines that start with `#` are comments. Read when the scenario is loaded.

samples.description: How many samples the table was made from. Written by the loader.

scale.description:
The factor, in thousandths, by which the entries were scaled down so that they fit 16 bits, and by which the `amount` of
the jitter is scaled up when it goes to `netem`. 1000 (or left out) when the samples reach at most 4 standard
deviations. Written by the loader.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file. Written by the loader; if it is in the file, the content of the file must match it.

values.description: The 4096 entries, as 4 hexadecimal digits each. Written by the loader; a scenario with the entries needs no file.

DelayTable.description:
The delay table of a jitter with `distribution: table`: where the samples came from and the table made of them.

In a scenario file only `file` is written. When the scenario is loaded the file is read and the other fields are filled
in, so that the canonical form of the scenario (and its hash) holds the table and the fingerprint of the file, and a
recorded scenario runs without the file (D-083). `sha256` may be written as well: then the file must have exactly that
content.

Direction.description: The side of a link that an event acts on.

oneOf.description: From the first node of `between` to the second.
From the second node to the first.
Both directions.

file.description: The file, a path relative to the directory of the scenario file. Read when the scenario is loaded.

format.description: `csv` or `mahimahi`. Left out, a name that ends in `.csv` is a CSV file.

period.description:
CSV only: how long one pass of the trace is, from its start to where it begins again. Default: the last row lasts as long
as the row before it.

points.description: The points. Written by the loader; a scenario with them needs no file.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file. Written by the loader; if it is in the file, the content must match it.

window.description:
Mahimahi only: how many milliseconds of the trace make one rate. The opportunities of a window are counted and give its
rate; a whole number of milliseconds. Default `100ms`.

DirectionTrace.description:
The trace of one direction of a link: the file it comes from and, once the file is read, the points.

In a scenario file `file` is written, with `format` unless the name ends in `.csv`, `window` for a Mahimahi trace and
`period` for a CSV file. The loader fills in the rest. `sha256` may be written as well: then the file must have exactly that
content.

Discipline.description: How the packets that wait for the rate are kept and dropped.

oneOf.description: A first-in first-out queue that drops what does not fit (`pfifo`, or `bfifo` with a limit in bytes). The default.
`CoDel` (RFC 8289): drops by the time a packet has waited.
FQ-CoDel (RFC 8290): a queue for each flow, each kept short by `CoDel`.
PIE (RFC 8033): drops by a probability that follows the delay of the queue.

access.description: The values of the link of each host to its router; its forward direction is from the host to the router.

bottleneck.description: The values of the link `bottleneck` between the two routers; its forward direction is from left to right.

left.description: The hosts on the left: at least one. They are joined to the router `router-left`.

right.description: The hosts on the right: at least one. They are joined to the router `router-right`.

Dumbbell.description: Hosts on two sides of a shared link between two routers.

Duration.description: A length of time: a number and a unit (ns, us, ms, s, m, h), a whole number of nanoseconds.

at.description: The moment, from the start of the measured phase. Before the end of it.

count.description: How many times the event happens in all. Needs `every`; not with `until`.

direction.description: For an `outage`: the direction it acts on. Both by default.

down.description: The interface of the link goes down: the sender gets errors (D-039).

every.description:
Repeats the event every so often, the first time at `at` (TML-03). Until `until` or for `count` times; with neither, until
the end of the measured phase.

outage.description:
Nothing is delivered for this long, not even a packet that is on its way, and the sender notices nothing
(D-039, D-064). It is a window in the time of the receiver: from this moment on, for this long, nothing
leaves the link. It does not change the values of the link, which act as before, and the packets that
reach the end of the link in the window are lost.

set.description:
Changes values of the link from this moment on. A key that is not written stays as it is, and `null`
takes the impairment away (the rule of a JSON merge patch).

until.description: The moment before which the event repeats. Needs `every`; not with `count`.

up.description: The interface of the link comes up again.

Event.description:
One event of the timeline: at a moment, one thing happens to a link. It does exactly one of `set`,
`outage`, `down` and `up`.

A `set`, a `down` and an `up` are applied before the first packet that its workload sends at or after the moment
(D-038), so the same seed gives the same lost packets; an `outage` is placed by the clock (D-064). Events at the
same moment are applied in the order of the file.

New keys are added to this type in later releases: make one with the constructors of the builder or read a file. (It is
`non_exhaustive` since the keys of a repeating event came, which was a break of its own.)

FlowProtocol.description: The transport protocol of a flow in a capture.

oneOf.description: UDP.
TCP.

dst.description: The address the packets go to.

dst-port.description: The port the packets go to.

src.description: The address the packets come from.

src-port.description: The port the packets come from.

FlowSelection.description:
Which flow of a capture is the trace: the packets that go from `src` to `dst`. What is left out is not asked about. When the
capture has only one flow nothing needs to be said; when it has several, the message lists them.

FormatVersion.description: The version of the scenario format. Version 0 is the series before 1.0 and may change in any minor release.

corrupt.description:
The chance that one bit of a packet is flipped (`netem corrupt`). A receiver with the UDP checksum
on drops the packet (D-040).

duplicate.description: The chance that a packet is sent twice (`netem duplicate`). The copy is impaired on its own.

loss.description: Packet loss: independent, or in bursts.

queue.description:
The queue in front of the rate: its size and how it drops (D-082). A link with a queue is built through the fabric of the
run (D-079).

rate.description: A limit on the data rate (`netem rate`).

reorder.description:
Packets that are sent on at once while the others are held back for the delay (`netem reorder`).
Needs `delay`.

Impairments.description: What a direction of a link does to the packets. Everything that is not set is not impaired.

ImpairmentsChange.description:
A change of the impairments of one direction. For each key: not written, the value stays; a value, it is
replaced as a whole (a `loss` replaces the loss, it does not merge into it); `null`, the impairment is
taken away. The result must be a valid set of impairments (a `jitter` needs a `delay`), and the reader
checks it for every step.

IpFamily.description: The family of the addresses that a flow uses.

oneOf.description: IPv4: a header of 20 bytes.
IPv6: a header of 40 bytes, and 8 more on a fragment.

IpMode.description:
Which addresses the network has. IPv6 in a namespace is not quiet (a few packets of its own in the first second), so a
network has it only where the scenario asks (D-081).

oneOf.description: IPv4 only. The default.
IPv6 only: the links and the nodes have no IPv4 address.
Both: every link and every node has an address of each family.

amount.description:
How much the delay varies: the delay lies within this amount above and below the fixed delay
(`uniform`), or this is the scale of the table that `netem` draws from: the standard deviation for `normal` and
`table`, the scale of the shipped table for `pareto` and `paretonormal`.

table.description:
The table of a `distribution: table` (D-084), made from a file of samples. In a step of the timeline it is left out:
the step changes the amount, and the table stays the one of the link.

Jitter.description:
Variation of the delay.

Not `Copy`: a table holds its entries (D-083). `non_exhaustive` so that a field can be added later without a break.

JitterDistribution.description: The distribution of the variation of the delay.

oneOf.description: Every delay between delay minus amount and delay plus amount is equally likely.
A bell curve around the delay, cut at about four standard deviations.

A heavy tail towards longer delays (the table `pareto` of iproute2). Added after the others because the order of the
variants is the order of the first releases.
A bell curve with a heavy tail towards longer delays (the table `paretonormal` of iproute2).
The shape of a file of samples (the `table` of the jitter).

between.description: The two nodes. `forward` is the direction from the first to the second.

both.description: The same impairments in both directions. Cannot be combined with `forward` or `reverse`.

cost.description: What the link costs the automatic routing: the shortest path is the smallest sum. 1 by default.

forward.description: The impairments from the first node to the second.

model.description:
How the link changes over time: a periodic pattern or a Markov chain (LMD-05, LMD-04, D-090). The values above are what the
link has outside the states.

mtu.description:
The MTU of the interface at both ends of the link, in bytes (D-081). 1500 by default. A datagram that does not fit
the first link of its path is cut into fragments by the sender; later links must carry those whole.

reverse.description: The impairments from the second node to the first.

Link.description: A link between two nodes, with the impairments of each direction.

begin.description: When the model begins, from the start of the measured phase. Before that the link is what the file says. Default `0s`.

both.description: Trace only: one trace for both directions. Not together with `forward` or `reverse`.

forward.description: Trace only: the trace of the direction from the first node to the second.

repeat.description:
Periodic and trace: whether the list of states, or the trace, begins again when it is over (the default), or the link is what
the file says after the last state (`false`).

reverse.description: Trace only: the trace of the direction from the second node to the first.

start.description: Markov only: the state the chain begins in. It is written, not drawn.

states.description:
The states. A periodic model goes through them in the order of the file; a Markov model needs at least two. A trace has
none.

LinkModel.description:
How a link changes over time: a periodic pattern, a Markov chain of states, or a trace from a file.

The keys of one kind are refused in the other, each at its own line. New keys are added to this type in later releases:
read a file to make one.

both.description: The same impairments in both directions.

cost.description: What the link costs the automatic routing. 1 by default.

forward.description: The impairments from the first node of the link to the second.

mtu.description: The MTU of the link in bytes. 1500 by default.

reverse.description: The impairments from the second node to the first.

LinkSpec.description: The values of a link that a shortcut makes: what a link has besides its name and its ends.

LinkTraceFormat.description: The format of the file of a trace of a link.

oneOf.description: A header and a row for each change, `time,rate,delay,loss`, every value with its unit.
One line for each opportunity to deliver a packet, the time in whole milliseconds (the format of Mahimahi).

Loss.description:
Packet loss. The model is chosen by `model`, and the parameters are those of `netem`, without aliases
(D-048).

It is read by hand (see `LossFields`), not by a derived reader for a tagged enum: that one collects the
mapping first, and an error in a value is then reported at the start of the mapping and not at the value.

p.description: The chance that a packet is lost.

oneOf.description: Every packet is lost with the same chance, independent of the others (`netem loss random`).

loss-bad.description: The chance that a packet is lost while in the bad state (the third argument of `gemodel`).

loss-good.description: The chance that a packet is lost while in the good state (the fourth argument of `gemodel`).

p.description: The chance, for each packet, to go from the good to the bad state.

r.description: The chance, for each packet, to go from the bad to the good state.

oneOf.description:
Two states, a good and a bad one, with a loss in each (`netem loss gemodel p r 1-h 1-k`). The mean
time in the bad state is `1 / r` packets. All four are required: a missing value would be a default
of `tc` that the file does not show.

Four states (`netem loss state p13 p31 p32 p23 p14`): 1 receiving in a gap, 2 receiving inside a
burst, 3 losing inside a burst, 4 losing a single packet in a gap. The numbers are the transitions
between the states they name. From state 1 the chances of `p13` and `p14` add up, and from state 3
those of `p31` and `p32`; neither sum may be above 100 %.

capture.description:
The links whose interfaces are captured, at both ends, as pcap files (PRB-09). A capture shows what the interface
carried after the queue, so a packet that the link dropped is in no file.

packets.description: Whether to write `packets-<id>.jsonl` with one line for each packet of each workload. Default `false`.

recovery.description: The time to recover after each event of the timeline.

series.description: The series of each workload by time bin.

Measure.description: What is measured and kept besides the statistics of each workload.

ModelKind.description: What kind of model a link has.

oneOf.description: A list of states that follow each other, each for a time that the file gives, and then again (LMD-05).
States with a mean time in each and the chances of the next one, drawn from the seed (LMD-04).

The rate, the delay and the loss over time from a file, for each direction (LMD-03, D-091). Last in the list because it was
added last.

direction.description: For an `outage`: the direction it acts on. Both by default.

distribution.description:
Markov only: whether the stay is exact (`fixed`) or drawn from an exponential distribution with `stay` as the mean
(the default).

down.description: The interface of the link is down while the state lasts (D-039).

for.description: Periodic only: how long the state lasts.

id.description: The name of the state. Required in a Markov model, where the chances refer to it.

outage.description: Nothing is delivered while the state lasts (D-064).

set.description: The values of the link while the state lasts.

stay.description: Markov only: how long the state lasts, or its mean (see `distribution`).

to.description: Markov only: the chances of the next state. They add up to 100 %, and none leads back to the state itself.

ModelState.description:
One state of a model.

It names what the link has while it lasts: a `set` (the keys of an impairment, as in a step of the timeline, a merge patch on
the link as the file writes it), an `outage`, or `down`. A state that writes none of them is the link as the file writes it.

from.description: The host that the forward direction of the links starts at.

Multipath.description: Two hosts joined by several paths, each over routers of its own.

Name.description: A name of 1 to 32 characters: lower case letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter and not ending with '-'.

Node.description: A node: its name (a host), or a mapping with the name and a role.

role.description: What the node does with packets that are not for it. A host by default.

NodeLong.description: The long form of a node in the schema.

OnExit.description:
What the run does when a program ends by itself before the end of the run, with an exit code other than 0 or by a
signal (D-072).

oneOf.description:
The run goes on to its end and the result reports how the program ended. The default: a program that crashes
under a bad network is a finding, not a fault of the tool.

The run is stopped with an error that names the program, how it ended and the end of its standard error. The
logs and the files of the run stay.

file.description: The file, a path relative to the directory of the scenario file. Read when the scenario is loaded.

format.description: `csv` or `pcap`. Left out, it is taken from the name of the file (`.csv`, `.txt`, `.pcap`, `.pcapng`, `.cap`).

packets.description: The packets. Written by the loader; a scenario with them needs no file.

padded.description:
How many packets of a capture were raised to the smallest payload that a packet of the agent can have (it carries a
header), such as an acknowledgement without data. Written by the loader.

select.description: For a capture with more than one flow: which one is the trace.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file. Written by the loader; if it is in the file, the content must match it.

PacketTrace.description:
The trace of a workload: the file it comes from, and, once the file is read, the packets.

In a scenario file only `file` is written (and `format` and `select` for a capture). When the scenario is loaded the rest is
filled in. `sha256` may be written as well: then the file must have exactly that content.

link.description: The values of every link of the path.

routers.description: The routers on the path from the first host to the second: at least one.

PathSpec.description: One path of a multipath: the routers it passes, in order, and the values of its links.

PhaseDistribution.description:
Whether the lengths of the phases of an on/off source, and the pauses between bursts, are exactly what the file says
or are drawn from an exponential distribution with that mean.

oneOf.description: Every phase lasts exactly the time given. The default: the source is a pattern you can calculate by hand.
The lengths are exponentially distributed with the time given as the mean (a Markov source).

Probability.description: A probability from 0% to 100% with at most six digits after the point. Always with the percent sign.

discipline.description: How the queue drops. `fifo` (the default), `codel`, `fq-codel` or `pie`.

ecn.description: Mark the packets of a flow that asked for it (ECN) instead of dropping them (`codel`, `fq-codel`, `pie`).

flows.description: The number of queues of `fq-codel`, one for each flow that hashes to it.

interval.description: The time over which `codel` and `fq-codel` look for a delay that does not go below the target.

limit.description: The size of the queue: packets (`100p`) or data (`64kb`, a `fifo` only).

quantum.description: The bytes a queue of `fq-codel` may send in its turn.

t-update.description: The time between two updates of the drop probability of `pie`.

target.description: The delay the queue accepts (`codel`, `fq-codel`, `pie`): above it the queue starts to drop.

Queue.description:
The queue of a direction (D-082): how many packets wait for the rate and how they are dropped.

Everything that is not set is the default of the kernel for the discipline: 1000 packets for a `fifo`, `codel` and `pie`,
10240 for `fq-codel`, a target of 5 ms and an interval of 100 ms for `CoDel`, 15 ms and a `t-update` of 15 ms for PIE. The
result records what was built.

QueueLimit.description: The size of the queue: a number of packets (100p) or an amount of data (64kb). Only a fifo counts bytes.

Rate.description: A data rate in bits per second, greater than zero: a number and a decimal unit (bit, kbit, mbit, gbit, tbit).

delay.description: Ready after this time, whatever the program does. The one way that checks nothing.

file.description: This file exists, a path relative to the directory of the scenario file.

stdout-line.description: A line of the standard output of the program contains this text.

tcp-port.description: A TCP socket listens in the node (read from `/proc/net/tcp`).

udp-port.description: A UDP socket is bound in the node, to any address or to its own (read from `/proc/net/udp`).

within.description: How long to wait for the program to become ready.

Ready.description:
How the run learns that a program is ready: exactly one of the five ways. The first four need `within`,
the time after which a program that is not ready counts as failed.

RecoveryBasis.description: The view the level of a bin is made from for the time to recover (see `docs/RESULTS.md`).

oneOf.description: Of the packets sent in a bin, the share that arrived (in the bin or later).
Of the packets sent in a bin, the share the receiver got in that bin (at most all of them).

baseline-bins.description: How many bins before the disturbance make the baseline level. Default 5.

basis.description: The view the level of a bin is made from: `send` (default) or `arrival`.

fraction.description: The share of the baseline that has to be reached again, above 0 % and at most 100 %. Default 90 %.

window-bins.description: How many bins in a row have to be back at the level. Default 3.

RecoverySettings.description: How the time to recover after an event is worked out. Every key has a default, so a section can name only what it changes.

gap.description:
After a packet that was sent on at once, the next `gap - 1` packets are held back before another one
can be sent on at once; 1 (the default) means no such rule. At least 1.

share.description: The chance that a packet is sent on at once.

Reorder.description:
Reordering by holding packets back (`netem reorder P gap G`).

With a `delay`, a share of the packets is sent on at once and the others wait for the delay, so the ones
that wait arrive after later packets. Measured in D-048: `share` is the share sent on at once, and with
`gap` it is `1 / (gap - 1 + 1 / share)`.

cc.description: The congestion control of the sockets: `cubic` (default), `reno`, `bbr` or another that the machine has.

connections.description: How many connections, from 1 to 1024. Default 1.

from.description: The node that sends the requests.

id.description: The name of the workload. Metrics are named after it.

interval.description:
The time between two requests of the whole workload (an open loop). Without it each connection sends the next request
when the response has arrived (a closed loop).

ip.description: The family of the addresses of the flow: `v4` or `v6`. Default: the only family of the network.

kind.description: `request-response`: requests of one size answered with responses of another, over TCP.

request.description: The size of a request, from 1 byte to 1 GiB.

response.description: The size of a response, from 1 byte to 1 GiB.

start.description: When the workload starts, from the start of the measured phase. Default `0s`.

stop.description: When the workload stops: no request is started after it. Default: the end of the measured phase.

timeout.description: How long a request waits for its response before it counts as failed. Default `30s`.

Role.description: What a node does with packets that are not for it.

oneOf.description: An end system: it sends and receives, and does not forward. The default.
It forwards packets between its links.

metric.description: The preference: the smaller is used first. 100 by default.

node.description: The node that has the route.

to.description:
The destination: a node (its address on the loopback of the node) or `default` for every destination that has no
route of its own.

via.description:
The link that the packets leave by; the node at its other end is the next hop. A link and not a neighbour, so that
two links between the same nodes are told apart.

weight.description: The share of a multipath route, 1 by default. Routes with the same metric share the packets by their weights.

Route.description:
A route of a node: to a destination, out of one of its links. Several routes of the same node and destination form a
failover (different metrics: the smallest is used while its link is up) or a multipath (the same metric, shared by
`weight`).

Routing.description: How the routes of the nodes come about.

oneOf.description:
The tool computes a route from every node to every node by the shortest path (the sum of the `cost` of the links,
1 by default), and the routes that are listed add to those or replace the routes of the same node and
destination. The default.
Only the listed routes exist.

bin.description: The width of a bin. Default `1s`. At least `1ms`, and the measured phase may have at most a million bins.

SeriesSettings.description: The series of each workload by time bin.

within.description: How long the program has to end. 5 seconds by default.

Shutdown.description:
How a program is stopped at the end of the run: the signal goes to its process group, and `KILL` follows
when it is still there after `within`.

Signal.description: A signal that asks a program to end. `KILL` is not among them: it is what follows when they do not work.

oneOf.description: `SIGTERM`.
`SIGINT`, what Ctrl-C sends.
`SIGHUP`.
`SIGQUIT`.
`SIGUSR1`.
`SIGUSR2`.

Size.description: An amount of data in bytes: a number and a unit (b, kb, mb, gb decimal; kib, mib, gib binary), a whole number of bytes.

hub.description: The name of the hub (a router).

leaves.description: The hosts around it: at least two. Each link is between a leaf and the hub, so its forward direction is towards the hub.

link.description: The values of every link, unless `links` has its own.

links.description: The values of the link of each leaf in turn, instead of `link`.

Star.description: A hub that is a router, with hosts around it.

TableValues.description: The 4096 entries of a delay table, each as 4 hexadecimal digits (two's complement, 8192 is one standard deviation). Written by the loader from the file of samples.

bytes.description: The payload that each connection sends. Without it each sends from `start` until `stop`.

cc.description: The congestion control of the sending sockets: `cubic` (default), `reno`, `bbr` or another that the machine has.

connections.description: How many connections, from 1 to 1024. Default 1.

id.description: The name of the workload. Metrics are named after it.

ip.description: The family of the addresses of the flow: `v4` or `v6`. Default: the only family of the network.

kind.description: `tcp-bulk`: data over TCP as fast as the network allows.

start.description: When the workload starts, from the start of the measured phase. Default `0s`.

stop.description: When the workload stops. Default: the end of the measured phase.

Template.description: A template (D-093): the parameters it takes and the content that a place of use is replaced by.

chain.description: A line of nodes: hosts at the ends, routers between.

dumbbell.description: Hosts on two sides of a link between two routers.

ecmp.description: With `auto`: install every equally short path as a multipath route, not only the first. Off by default.

ip.description: The addresses the network has: `v4` (the default), `v6` or `dual`.

links.description: The links between the nodes. Two nodes may have several. Not together with a shortcut.

multipath.description: Two hosts joined by several paths over routers of their own.

nodes.description: The nodes: a name for a host, or `{ id, role }`. Not together with a shortcut.

routing.description: How the routes come about: `auto` (the default) or `manual`.

star.description: A router with hosts around it.

Topology.description:
The nodes, the links and the routes of a scenario.

In a file the nodes and links are written out, or given as one of the shortcuts `chain`, `star`, `dumbbell` and
`multipath` (D-078), which are expanded when the file is read: what is held and written again is always the long form.

TraceData.description: The packets of a trace: for each packet the time since the packet before and the payload in bytes, each as a LEB128 number, written as hexadecimal. Written by the loader from the file of the trace.

TraceFormat.description: The format of the file of a trace.

oneOf.description:
A text file with one packet on each line: the time since the start and the payload, each with its unit
(`12.5ms,1200b`).

A capture of the packets of a real flow (`pcap` or `pcapng`): the transport payload of the packets of one flow, at the
moments they were captured.

UdpChecksum.description:
Whether the packets of a [`UdpCbr`] carry a UDP checksum.

With the checksum on (the default) a receiver drops a packet whose bits were flipped on the way, as on a
real network. With it off the damaged packet arrives, and the result counts it as `corrupted` (D-040).

In a file it is a boolean, `udp-checksum: false`, and not the words `on` and `off`: YAML 1.1 reads those as
booleans (`PyYAML`, `yamllint` and some editors do), YAML 1.2 as text, and a file must mean one thing in both.

Workload.description:
A workload: something that runs in a node. Either a generator that sends traffic ([`UdpCbr`],
[`UdpPoisson`], [`UdpOnOff`], [`UdpBursty`]), or the program that is being tested ([`Command`]).

It is read by hand (see `WorkloadFields`) for the reason that `Loss` is: the derived reader for a tagged
enum reports an error in a value at the start of the mapping and not at the value.

More kinds come in later releases, so a `match` outside this crate needs a wildcard arm.

description: A scenario: a network, what runs in it, and for how long.

allow-limited.description:
